source: Blue Zones (Dan Buettner / National Geographic) — the five regions with verified highest concentrations of centenarians.
note: Longevity ground-truth overlay. Per the canon thesis longevity is an OUTCOME (downstream of the biophysics branch), not a foundation — used here to validate world-indicator rankings against where people actually live longest.

zones.title: Okinawa, Japan
zones.longevity_note: World's longest-lived women; diet of sweet potato, tofu, bitter melon; 'ikigai' (sense of purpose) and 'moai' (lifelong social circles).

zones.title: Nuoro / Ogliastra, Sardinia, Italy
zones.longevity_note: Highest concentration of male centenarians; mountain shepherding (daily movement), pecorino, Cannonau wine, strong family elder-care.

zones.title: Nicoya Peninsula, Costa Rica
zones.longevity_note: Lowest middle-age mortality; 'plan de vida' (purpose), calcium-rich water, beans/corn/squash, sunshine and strong faith/community.

zones.title: Ikaria, Greece
zones.longevity_note: 'The island where people forget to die'; Mediterranean diet, wild greens, herbal teas, afternoon naps, low rates of dementia.

zones.title: Loma Linda, California, USA
zones.longevity_note: Seventh-day Adventist community living ~10 years longer than other Americans; plant-based diet, sabbath rest, no smoking/alcohol, tight community.
